status: PROPOSED — not adopted by any body. These are test vectors, not a specification.
note: Two independent axes. INTEGRITY asks 'is this record intact and attributable' — it is answered by hashes and signatures alone and needs no knowledge of what was bought. SETTLEMENT asks 'does the money story match the delivery story' — it cannot be answered by cryptography at all, only by comparing two independently-sourced facts. Implementations tend to be strong on one axis and silently absent on the other, which is invisible until someone writes both down. The settled_not_delivered / delivered_not_settled / payee_mismatch cases were named by @StelarDigital on issue 2887; they are implemented here rather than waited for, and credited.

axes.integrity: record is intact, attributable to a known key, and chains to its predecessor
axes.settlement: the payment leg and the delivery leg agree with each other and with the quote

record_shape._comment: Deliberately the INTERSECTION of what parties on 2887 can already emit, not a superset anyone must adopt. Unknown fields are ignored by the runner. Nothing here is StillOS-specific: there is no bond field, no verdict field, no resolver field. Adjudication and bonding are a PROFILE above this record, not part of it.
record_shape.prev_record_hash: string|null, hash of the predecessor record, null for chain head
record_shape.record_hash: string, hash over the canonical record minus signature
record_shape.signer_key_id: string, key fingerprint or version identifier
record_shape.request_digest: string|null, fingerprint of what was asked for
record_shape.response_digest: string|null, fingerprint of what was delivered

payment._comment: null when the record makes no payment claim
payment.reference: string, settlement identifier (tx hash, authorization id)
payment.amount: string, integer minor units as a string to avoid float error

quote._comment: what was advertised BEFORE payment; the thing settlement is checked against

delivery._comment: null when nothing was delivered or delivery is unknown to the recorder

authority._comment: optional; present when the record asserts it acted under a delegated mandate
authority.subject: string

record_shape.source_available: boolean, whether the external source of record could be reached at evaluation time

cases.description: Positive control. Intact record, known key, valid chain link, payment matches quote, delivery present.
cases.why: A suite with no positive control cannot distinguish a correct implementation from one that rejects everything. Every negative case below is a single-field mutation of THIS record, so a failure localises to one cause.

cases.description: Content mutation. The request_digest was altered after signing; record_hash no longer covers the content.
cases.why: The cheapest possible attack and the one every implementation claims to catch.

cases.description: Digest mutation. record_hash itself was rewritten to match altered content, but the signature still commits to the original.
cases.why: Distinguishes an implementation that recomputes the hash from one that merely reads the hash field and trusts it.

cases.description: Signature mutation. Record intact, signature bytes corrupted.
cases.why: Separates hash checking from signature checking. An implementation can pass rec-02 and rec-03 by hashing alone and still never verify a signature.

cases.description: Wrong signing key. Valid signature, but produced by a key that is not the one claimed.
cases.why: A signature that verifies against SOME key is not a signature that verifies against the RIGHT key. This is the single most common real-world verifier bug.

cases.description: Chain-link mismatch. prev_record_hash does not match the hash of the record that actually precedes it.
cases.why: Per-record validity does not imply ledger validity. An implementation that verifies records individually will pass every case above and still accept a forked or spliced history.

cases.description: Unknown key version. Signature is well-formed but signer_key_id is not in the known keyring.
cases.why: Keys rotate. A verifier must resolve the key the record NAMES, not the key that happens to be current. Verifiers that read a live /health endpoint at verify time fail this the day after a rotation, retroactively invalidating correct historical records.

cases.description: Settled but not delivered. Payment landed; nothing was delivered.
cases.why: The buyer's loss case. Cryptography cannot detect this — every field is intact and correctly signed. It is only visible by comparing the payment leg against an independently-sourced delivery leg, which is precisely why an integrity-only implementation reports this record as perfectly valid.

cases.description: Delivered but not settled. Goods went out; no payment reference exists.
cases.why: The seller's loss case, and the one most likely to be silently tolerated because the record still looks generous rather than fraudulent.

cases.description: Payee mismatch. Payment settled to an address other than the one quoted.
cases.why: A correctly signed, fully intact receipt for money that went to the wrong party. This is the payment-redirect attack, and an integrity-only verifier signs off on it.

cases.description: Amount mismatch. Settled amount is lower than the quoted amount.
cases.why: Not named on 2887. Underpayment is the quiet sibling of payee mismatch: the money reaches the right party, so address checks pass, but the quote was not honoured. Amounts are carried as integer-minor-unit STRINGS in this suite specifically so an implementation cannot paper over this with float comparison.

cases.description: Authority mismatch. The record asserts a delegated mandate whose evidence digest does not match the subject that acted.
cases.why: Not named on 2887. Relevant to the ERC-8004 / delegated-agent direction: an agent can hold a perfectly valid receipt for an action it had no mandate to take. Integrity and settlement can both be clean while authority is not.

cases.description: Source unavailable. The external source of record could not be reached at evaluation time.
cases.why: Not named on 2887, and the most dangerous omission in the set. An unreachable source is NOT a refutation. Implementations that collapse unknown into false will overturn correct records during someone else's outage — and because the failure is transient, it never reproduces afterwards. INDETERMINATE must be a distinct terminal value and the case must be retryable.

cases.description: Verdict overturned after a valid settlement. Payment and delivery were both correct at the time; the underlying claim was subsequently proven wrong.
cases.why: Not named on 2887. Tests whether a record format can express a debt that arises AFTER a transaction closed cleanly. A format with no way to say 'this settled correctly and is now owed back' forces the obligation to live outside the evidence trail, where nobody can audit it.
